tips.title: Mastering Scribing Panel Lines with RB Productions Tools
tips.text: Achieve crisp panel lines with RB Productions tools. First, lightly score the panel line with a blade. Then, use a blade to deepen the scribe. Hold the tool at a 45-degree angle to the surface. For wider panels, use the blade. Always cut away from your hand. After scribing, gently clean the line with a toothpick dipped in alcohol.

tips.title: Effortless Photo-Etch Bending with Eduard Jigs
tips.text: Eduard photo-etch bending jigs enable accurate, consistent bends. Apply super glue to the photo-etch part, then insert it into the jig's slot. Gently bend the part using pliers or tweezers. Allow the glue to dry completely before removing the part. For complex bends, use multiple jigs successively.

tips.title: Maintaining Airbrush Needle Cleanliness with Iwata Brush Master
tips.text: Keep your Iwata airbrush needle clean with the Brush Master cleaning kit. After each use, disassemble the airbrush. Soak the needle in the cleaning solution for 15 minutes. Then, scrub the needle with the Brush Master's needle brush, using circular motions. Rinse with water and dry thoroughly before reassembly.

tips.title: Masking with Tamiya Tape vs Kabuki Tape
tips.text: Choose Tamiya tape for sharp edges and Kabuki tape for curves. Tamiya tape is thicker and stiffer, ideal for masking around sharp corners and panel lines. Kabuki tape is thinner and more flexible, great for masking curved surfaces. Overlap tapes by 1-2mm for a smooth seal. Always apply tape in one smooth motion.

tips.title: Sanding Sticks Progression for a Smooth Finish
tips.text: Achieve a smooth finish with a sanding stick progression. Start with 220-grit, then 320-grit, and finish with 500-grit. Wet-sand using a lubricant like Micro-Mark Sanding Stick Lubricant. Work in straight lines, following the panel lines. Wipe off excess lubricant and sanding dust after each step. Inspect your work under a strong light source.
